121	the Holy Land, as it's called,
122	there is something here. There is in this a
123	Divine matter, a spiritual matter. It's a matter that touches each
124	one in his own soul.
125	The division is not only the division of land, where the Jewish people
126	each received his portion. It is actually
127	the division of the mission of each one. Each tribe had
128	its own special mission, each family had its
129	special mission, and each and every person has
130	this special mission. And this is the wonderful message:
131	that HaShem performed this wondrous miracle,
132	which gives us the picture
133	of how we will know what our mission is and how we will behave
134	and live with our mission.
135	But let's first lay down a introduction.
136	We know that no two people are the same. Just as
137	their faces are not alike, their opinions are not alike.
138	Their character traits are not equal, their fingerprints are not
139	equal, our fingerprints, which are one centimeter,
140	and let's see something wonderful: in that one centimeter
141	how many possibilities there can be. There never were two people,
142	nor will there be, among the billions and billions of
143	people who exist and who have existed, who have
144	two identical fingerprints. A wonder of wonders.
145	And so it is very important that each one of us
146	be aware of his special qualities.
147	He needs to know the gift that HaShem gave him. And I
148	know that there are people who, out of humility, say: "I have nothing,
149	no, no, no, no, that's not true, it's the opposite."
150	The moment you are not aware of the gifts, it is ingratitude.
151	HaShem gave you the gifts. HaShem gave you a good
152	mind. A good heart, sensitivity,
153	a sense
154	of helping another, a sense of prayer, whatever it is, and you
155	don't thank HaShem. This has nothing to do with
156	pride, because you didn't do it. Don't take
157	credit for it.
158	It's not a credit for you. It obligates you
159	to act. HaShem gave you the strength, you need to
160	use it.
161	There is a saying I heard in the name of the Baal Shem Tov, I didn't see
162	it written, that he says: what is Gehinnom?
163	Gehinnom is a state where a person goes, after 120 years,
164	to the heavens
165	and sees what he could have been, what he could
166	have done, the enormous potential he had,
167	and suddenly he feels: I wasted it, I threw it
168	in the trash. That is the greatest Gehinnom. And therefore each one
169	must be aware, must have the grasp,
170	the understanding: what are my qualities? I think I once
171	told this about the Rebbe Rashab, a relative of the Rebbe's.
172	The Rebbe Rashab once held a farbrengen and spoke words
173	of enormous wisdom, and then someone said to him: Rashab, you are
174	so profound, so wise, have you ever made a mistake
175	in your life? He says: yes. In what did you make a mistake? He says:
176	in my qualities. I said to him: you have many
177	qualities, don't be humble, you have many qualities. He says:
178	no, no, you didn't understand me. I didn't mean
179	that I made a mistake by thinking I have many qualities
180	and I don't. The opposite. I thought I had fewer, and I have
181	more. The Rebbe Rashab said to his son: this is the way of
182	Chassidut. Know your qualities, but know that it
183	obligates you. And this is what is written: Jacob saw a ladder
184	set on the earth with its top reaching the heavens. And behold, angels of
185	Elokim ascending and descending on it.
186	The commentators ask: it should have been the opposite. Behold, angels of
187	Elokim descending, they are in heaven,
188	and afterwards ascending. What is the meaning of ascending and descending?
189	So the Midrash says: they ascended on high to the lofty levels
190	and they saw that Jacob's image is engraved
191	on the Throne of Glory.
192	They descended below and see him sleeping.
193	The ministering angels sought to harm Jacob.
194	They see what he could be,
195	and they look here, and with their own eyes they did not see
196	his greatness. So how do you miss such
197	potential, such enormous potential that HaShem gave him?
198	That is to say, each one needs to be aware,
199	aware of what you can be, of your potential.
200	And this is not the time to be humble: "I have nothing, I'm not
201	successful, I can't." The opposite. "And his heart was lifted
202	in the ways of HaShem." Be aware of this and thank
203	HaShem. There is a verse: "Honor HaShem
204	with your substance."
205	With what He graced you.
206	You need to honor HaShem, to use
207	what He graced you with, what He gave you.
208	So the Midrash says: He gave you a son, make him a brit
209	milah. He gave you a house, put up the mezuzah. He gave you
210	a courtyard, build a sukkah.
211	The Midrash says: if you had a sweet voice,
212	be the one who says Shema Yisrael out loud and be
213	a chazan.
214	You need to honor HaShem with your substance. What is "your substance"?
215	What He actually graced you with. Everyone must think about
216	his qualities. And not only that: if he doesn't know,
217	ask your good friend. Ask about your qualities.

219	And with us, we have
220	a yeshivah of young men,
221	and many times I gather them and say: each
222	one should write three or five qualities about his friend.
223	When you tell him, "write about yourself," he is embarrassed.
224	Write about your friend. And afterwards each one gives the
225	letter to his neighbor, and people open up so much, they
226	receive so much strength and power.
227	The Gemara comes and says, the Midrash of Reish Lakish: the world was not
228	fit to use gold. Why is gold needed in the world? You need
229	food, you need water. Why is gold needed? Why was it created?
230	For the Mishkan, or it is written, for the Beit HaMikdash.
231	The Rebbe says something wonderful:
232	Gold is a luxury. You don't need it
233	in order to live.
234	There are things a person needs
235	in the world in order to live: intellect, heart, health, and so on
236	and so on. But every person must think: what do I have
237	that is a luxury? Gold is a luxury.
238	What do I have that is above the average,
239	above what a person needs in order to live?
